text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 1.84% today, extending a sharp 7.55% decline over two weeks. The main driver is a shift in market sentiment around refining stocks: a major financial outlet reported today that "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding," signaling investors are rotating out of the sector after an extended run-up. This comes even though refineries are running at a healthy 95.7% capacity and oil inventories remain relatively stable.

The timing matters because geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries and Iranian-backed drone strikes—have created uncertainty about regional oil supply, yet this risk no longer appears to be supporting refiner valuations the way it did earlier in the year. With climate negotiations failing to curb fossil fuel use and the broader energy trade losing momentum, the tailwind that lifted refining stocks has reversed.
